title: Browser approval gates
summary: A recipe step typed operator_gate machine_browser_approval approves the installer's one-time code in the test machine's own signed-in browser: Safari on macOS, the desktop Chromium on Linux and WSL. Every driver shares one matcher: only the installer-opened tab on the declared origin with the displayed code, revalidated before Approve machine is pressed, and only a same-origin navigation away from it counts. On Linux the gate runs xdg-settings get default-web-browser inside a login shell, the same read the Machine QA provisioner uses, and starts Chromium with that shell's XDG_DATA_DIRS; a bare SSH environment is not consulted. It then starts the desktop and Chromium with a loopback DevTools port and runs the installer on that desktop; the step always attaches a desktop screenshot. A host without a desktop refuses headless_linux_browser_approval_unavailable. A login shell that cannot print XDG_DATA_DIRS refuses linux_desktop_session_environment_unavailable. Both name the provisioning recovery. A setup that exits before or during approval fails the gate as terminal_setup_exited with its exit code and printed refusal, not as missing approval context.
